phase1b_complete.summary: Every entry-file operation follows one pattern. Decide and take splitDNSRepair.queue() in the owner turn, then platformWork.run in that same turn. Inside the block, the operation and its residue read (Observation.after) run in one resolvers.serialized scope against the operation's own config. The owner then records with await recordSplitDNS(observation, source:, startedAt: place). Gate-driven work (VPN transitions and the two post-write corrections) goes through reconcileEntryFiles(config:runtimeStarted:). No blocking manager or file read is left on the owner.
phase1b_complete.r1_design_carried_unchanged: Every r1 design point in author-test-migration.json 'design' stands: same-turn enqueue at every site; runtimeStarted = true in the continueStart turn; Stop freshness by queue place (startedAt < generation); a refused removal is kept; recordInterceptRefresh(failed:place:); files before orchestrator; legacy compositions (SplitDNSVPNGate.reconcileEntryFiles, SplitDNSEntryFileRepair.retry, record's optional startedAt) kept for pm-sim and the unit tests.

1_start_residue_before_its_sweep.defect_in_r1: applyProxySurfaces read Observation.after before the refreshInterceptFiles sweep in the same resolvers.serialized scope. A recorded file for a disabled intercept rule counted as residue although the start's sweep (clearInterceptFiles, forCleanup: true) removed it, so a pending repair the start fixed stayed pending, and markResolverSwitchLanded waited for a later retry.
1_start_residue_before_its_sweep.fix: RuntimeHost.swift applyProxySurfaces: the Observation.after read moved to after the sweep's do/catch, still inside the same resolvers.serialized scope (same lock, same block, same queue place). This matches the config-change block, which already reads residue after its refresh.

2_drop_and_reconnect_during_start_block.defect_in_r1: Sequence: the start's block captures vpnConnected = true; a drop, handled with runtimeStarted false, queues a .remove behind the start's apply; the reconnect, still with runtimeStarted false, decides .nothing; the tail compares the net gate state (wanted == captured) and does not correct. Result: tunnel up, runtime started, no entry file, and no failure recorded for a retry. Reachable while observers already run during a proxy start (DNS module up, or a restart).
2_drop_and_reconnect_during_start_block.fix: RuntimeHost.swift applyProxySurfaces: gateReportSeen = splitDNSGateOrder.applied is captured in the same turn as vpnConnected. The tail corrects when splitDNSGate.entriesWanted != vpnConnected || (splitDNSGate.entriesWanted && splitDNSGateOrder.applied != gateReportSeen). It uses the existing VPN report sequence (VPNObservationOrder.applied); no new state. The added case only queues an idempotent apply through reconcileEntryFiles(config:runtimeStarted: true), decided and queued in the runtimeStarted = true turn, so same-turn enqueue, Stop freshness and runtimeStarted placement are unchanged. The switch-on tail is unchanged: runtimeStarted is already true there, so a reconnect during its block applies itself.

cheap_fixes.DNSManager_lock_doc_preflight_correction: DNSManager.swift operations-lock comment: the claim that the activation preflight is a reader on another queue that the lock protects is removed. The comment now names launch recovery's own job (recoverLegacyOwnership) and direct callers of the type as what still overlaps the host's PlatformWork queue.
cheap_fixes.r1_manifest_statement_corrected: r1 risks_and_remaining said 'Readers on other queues (the activation preflight) still take the DNSManager lock'. That is wrong. Correct statement: the activation preflight reads DNSManager state from a global queue without its lock; nothing on the owner calls DNSManager after 1b; launch recovery calls it from its own job.
cheap_fixes.pm_sim_nonvacuous_drop_order: RuntimeHostEffectsScenarios.swift reloadAndStopWhileHeld: new witness dropLandedBeforeStopRestore and check 'once released, the drop's removal lands before the Stop's system proxy restore'. risks_and_remaining: Head-of-line latency (accepted, unmeasured): the orchestrator's VPN handling waits behind unrelated queued platformWork, because the entry files must land first. The owner stays free.

Redundant correction writes (accepted): both post-write corrections can queue an idempotent apply the VPN handler's own work would also cover. r2 widens the start tail by one case: any gate report taken while the block was out, with entries wanted, now costs one extra idempotent apply even when it did not flip the gate (for example connected to reasserting).
Intercept-refresh places leave harmless gaps in queue order, which newer= counts.
Residue is read against the operation's own config, not the host's accepted view at record time; at start it is now read after the start's intercept sweep.
Protection against priority-ordered resumption is verified by construction only, until the RuntimeActor retag.
The activation preflight reads DNSManager state from a global queue without its lock (unchanged since before 1b; documented at DNSManager.serialized).
